resources.string: Experimental. Bluetooth stays the way to hear phone calls on your computer; try this only if you want to test an alternative.
What it does, and the risks

This lets GeekBridge capture the audio of your phone calls through Wireless debugging and send it to a computer you choose. Wireless debugging gives the helper powers far beyond call audio: it can do what adb shell can do. Turn it off when you are done. Nothing is recorded or stored. Recording calls may be illegal where you live without the other person\'s consent. Samsung or your carrier may block it, and then you will only hear silence.
Off by default. Each call still needs your press on the computer.

On the phone: Settings, Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging (or USB debugging). On your computer run geekbridge-ctl callwifi setup and follow it: it pairs with the code the phone shows and starts the helper. The helper runs until you reboot the phone or run setup --stop.
Pairing from inside the app (without a computer) is not built yet.

First a check with no call (so silence can be told from sound; if that check is refused or delivers nothing, the answer will be Unsure, never Works), then a real call: the app listens to the call source for a few seconds and says whether the other person\'s voice gets through. Only levels are measured; nothing is kept.

The phone cannot tell by itself whether the other person hears audio put into the call. This plays short beeps through three possible routes: 1 beep, then 2 beeps, then 3 beeps. Ask the other person how many beeps they heard (warn them first), then tap the answer. Speak uses that route.
Only the computers you tick may ask to listen, and only during a call, after a press on that computer.
Let the computer\'s microphone be heard by the other person. Separate from listening; the other person may or may not hear it.
Needs a listening test that works and a speaking test the other person heard first.
Call audio is being shared with %1$s.
The computer\'s microphone is also sent into the call.
